gap: No result ChatGPT got says which mechanical keyboard-and-mouse combos run both devices off one 2.4 GHz receiver. The makers' stores say Redragon's BS8773 ($36.99) and S136 K628+M693 ($59.99) share one dongle, Redragon's $89.99 HORUS K618+M693 needs separate dongles, Keychron's $179.99 K2 HE+M3 bundle uses one dongle for both, and HyperX's $109.99 bundle pairs a wired keyboard with a wireless mouse.
standout_why: I read three of the rival pages. gamingreviewguide.com only says 'Wireless bundles use one USB receiver in some sets' and never names which. wikikeyboard.com lists 12 combos with prices and says nothing about shared dongles for any of them. mechkeyfoundry.com confirms a shared receiver only for the Logitech MX Mechanical + MX Master 3S pair, and lists Keychron's bundle as Q7+M3 Mini with no price and receiver sharing not stated. None of them covers the budget Redragon combos ChatGPT showed as cards. deskfinds.com returned 403, so I couldn't compare against it.
decides: For a shopper who wants a wireless mechanical set on one USB port, the Redragon S136 (K628 PRO + M693) is the cheapest true mechanical combo the maker confirms runs on one shared dongle: $59.99 at Redragon and $49.99 on Amazon today. The BS8773 is $23 cheaper at $36.99 but uses low-profile switches, a single blue backlight and a mouse that tops out at 2,400 DPI. The HORUS K618 combo costs more ($89.99) yet needs two dongles. The HyperX $109.99 bundle loses if both devices must be wireless, because its Alloy Origins Core is a wired USB-C keyboard. Above $150, Keychron's K2 HE + M3 ($179.99, one dongle) undercuts Logitech's MX Mechanical + MX Master 3S ($269.98 bought separately on logitech.com).
